name: Ticagrelor
summary: A directly acting, reversible P2Y12 inhibitor with faster and more potent platelet inhibition than clopidogrel for acute coronary syndromes.
mechanism: Directly and reversibly inhibits the platelet P2Y12 ADP receptor (not a prodrug), blocking ADP-mediated platelet activation and aggregation.
pharmacodynamics: Greater and more consistent platelet inhibition than clopidogrel; reduced CV death, MI, and stroke in ACS (PLATO).

pharmacokinetics.metabolism: Hepatic, primarily CYP3A4/3A5 to the active metabolite AR-C124910XX; P-gp substrate

dosing.adult: Loading 180 mg, then 90 mg twice daily (60 mg twice daily for extended therapy after 1 year post-MI)
dosing.renalAdjustment: No dose adjustment required for renal impairment (including dialysis)

contraindications: Concurrent strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole, clarithromycin)
warnings: Major bleeding including fatal intracranial hemorrhage
Bradyarrhythmias — avoid in sick sinus syndrome or high-grade AV block without pacemaker

clinicalPearls: Reversible binding means platelet function returns ~3–5 days after stopping.
Dyspnea is a distinctive side effect; rule out ischemia, but it is often benign.
good: ACS patients needing potent, rapid antiplatelet effect.
bad: Patients with prior intracranial hemorrhage, severe hepatic disease, or strong CYP3A4 inhibitor use.
